config.note: game_plot = authored arc (2 beats/week: a plot_call + a weekend life beat). daily_calls = tagged pool served per day.

prologue.title: First Shift
prologue.synopsis: Meet the floor and Martha. Set the tone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night one. The dispatch floor hums like a held breath — a wall of screens, a hundred blinking lines, and the quiet certainty that somewhere out there, someone is about to need you.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: You must be the rookie. Martha. Take the console next to mine — I'll keep you whole.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: One rule before the lines light up: not every voice on this frequency wants saving. Part of the job is learning the difference.

decision.prompt: First thing you say to your mentor

choices.label: I'm here to help all of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha smiles like she already knows which kind of dispatcher you'll be. The first line lights up.

plot_call.title: The Call That Drops
plot_call.synopsis: A girl, an address, dead air. Martha says prank.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A young woman's voice, low and fast, like she's not supposed to be on the phone.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Please — I'm at, it's the house on Calder, the blue one with the—

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The line goes dead. Not hung up. Taken away.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Dropped call. We get a dozen a night off that block — kids daring each other. Mark it closed, rookie.

decision.prompt: The line just died. What do you do?

choices.label: Martha knows the block. Mark it closed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You write the address on a sticky note. Calder Street, blue house. Probably nothing. You keep it anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Straight to a dead tone — the line's been pulled. But the call's logged now, with a timestamp Martha can't quietly erase.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Closed: prank, juvenile. Martha nods, pleased. Somewhere a blue house on Calder goes quiet again.

weekend.title: Thank You, From Maple Court
weekend.synopsis: Grandma calls to thank you. Lily is named.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Saturday. Your phone buzzes — the station forwarded a thank-you call.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Sweetheart, it's the lady from Maple Court — you sent help for my chest last week. I wanted a real person to hear me say thank you.

decision.prompt: Grandma's on the line on your day off

choices.label: Glad you're okay. Take care now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She tells you about her granddaughter Lily, who 'works too many late shifts.' You file the name away without knowing why.

plot_call.title: Same Block
plot_call.synopsis: Second call, same street. Martha reroutes the unit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tuesday graveyard. A different voice. The same fear.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: There's a house — girls go in, they don't, they don't come back out. I'm across the street, I can see—

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: It's 1411 Calder. One door down from the blue one.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I've got the nearest unit on a fender-bender two blocks over. Let me re-balance the board — I'll route this one when a car frees up.

decision.prompt: Martha wants to reroute the only nearby unit

choices.label: No — send a car to Calder now.
Note the address. Let her balance it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A unit rolls to 1411. They find a locked, empty house and an open back door. But it's in the system now — same block, twice. That's a pattern.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By the time a car frees up, there's nothing to find. You add 1411 to the sticky note. Two addresses now, one street.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha handles it her way. The board balances. The street stays a blur.

weekend.title: Coffee With Martha
weekend.synopsis: The friendship deepens — the trap baits itself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha texts: 'Coffee? You look like the job's already eating you.'

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I mean it about keeping you whole. I burned out two rookies before you. I'm not doing it again.

decision.prompt: Martha, off the clock, being genuinely kind

choices.label: Let her in. She's good company.
Ask why she really chose this job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She laughs at your jokes, pays for your coffee, and for one evening the city feels survivable. You almost forget the sticky note.

plot_call.title: The House on Calder
plot_call.synopsis: A neighbor's tip. First hard fork: act or defer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A neighbor's whisper, hand cupped around the receiver.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: The house on Calder. Curtains always shut. Vans at 3am. Girls I never see twice. I'm scared to give my name.

decision.prompt: A real tip. Your authority to dispatch.

choices.label: Send a welfare check now, on my authority.
Loop Martha in before I move.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You get it all down — times, plates, descriptions. A spine of a case forms on your screen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The car's already rolling. You'll write it up after.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Anonymous tip, no crime in progress, shy caller? That's a noise complaint, hon. Send a car and you'll spook a landlord, not save anyone. Let me file it soft.

choices.label: File it soft, like Martha says.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The unit reports a nervous man who won't open up and a house that's 'just movers.' No arrest. But it's the first official knock on that door — and the ring felt it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Filed soft. Buried in the noise tickets. You tell yourself Martha knows the city better than you. The pawn doesn't always see the board.

weekend.title: The Sticky Note
weekend.synopsis: Start a private file, or let it go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 3am. You can't sleep. The sticky note is still on your fridge. Two addresses. One street.

decision.prompt: What do you do with the note?

choices.label: Start a private file — dates, names, everything.
Throw it out. You're imagining patterns.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You build a quiet file Martha doesn't know about. It feels like paranoia. It feels like the only honest thing you've done all week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Into the trash. You sleep better. You shouldn't.

plot_call.title: The Envelope
plot_call.synopsis: Bribe under the keyboard. Take it or log it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: End of shift. There's an envelope tucked under your keyboard. Cash, and a note: 'For the dispatcher who knows when to look away. — a grateful friend.'

decision.prompt: An envelope of cash. Nobody saw it arrive.

choices.label: Log it as evidence. Tampering, bribery.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Oh, that. The city takes care of people who don't make waves. Keep it or don't — but if you turn it in, you're telling them you're a wave. Think about which is safer.

decision.prompt: Martha just told you who the envelope is from — without saying it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You bag it, photograph it, log it. Your hands shake. Now there's paper that says someone paid you to look away — and you said no.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The cash goes in your jacket. Warm, heavy, easy. You just learned the price of looking away. So did they.

weekend.title: Drive-By
weekend.synopsis: Look at the house, or look away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You stare at the ceiling. The block has a sound now — vans, curtains, dead air on a held breath.

choices.label: Pour a drink and forget it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Blue house, shut curtains, a van you memorize the plate of. You add it to the file. You're in it now, whether you meant to be or not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You drink until the street goes quiet in your head. It's still there in the morning.

plot_call.title: Grandma's Girl
plot_call.synopsis: Lily is missing. Calder Street. The stakes get a name.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A number you know. Grandma. But her voice is wrong — small, broken.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Lily didn't come home. Three nights. The police say she's a grown woman, she'll turn up. But she always calls me. Always.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Her last text said she got a new job. Bartending. Some place on Calder Street.

decision.prompt: The street. The name. It's someone you know now.

choices.label: Open a missing-person case myself. Right now.
Promise Grandma you'll find her — off the books.
Tell her to wait for the regular process.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You pull Lily's file into the system and tie it to Calder — formally, where Martha will see it. The horror has a name and a grandmother now. You can't unsee it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't log it where Martha can watch. You promise an old woman you'll bring her girl home. It's the most dangerous promise you've ever made.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You give her the script: 24 hours, file a report, wait. The line goes quiet. You've never hated the script more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You meet Grandma in person. A photo of Lily on the kitchen table — laughing, a new haircut, the late-shift job she was so proud of.

decision.prompt: Grandma asks you, point blank: is my girl in trouble?

choices.label: Tell her the truth as far as you know it.
Protect her. Say you're sure Lily's fine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You leave with the photo in your pocket and a face to put on the dead air. Calder Street isn't a pattern anymore. It's Lily.

plot_call.title: What Martha Types
plot_call.synopsis: Midpoint: you catch the inside man. It's her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 3am lull. You glance at Martha's screen to ask about a code — and freeze.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She's got Lily's case open. Status: reclassified — 'voluntary, no action.' And in a side window, she's typing an address into a text thread with no name. 1411 Calder.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: ...You're staring, rookie. Something on my screen interesting?

decision.prompt: You just saw the inside man. It's Martha. What now?

choices.label: Report it up the chain tonight.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Careful. You don't know what you saw, and you really don't know what you're standing in. I've kept you whole this far. Don't make me stop.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You look away, heart slamming. Later, in the bathroom, you photograph what you can from memory and add it to the file. She can't know you know.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You write it up for the night supervisor. By morning the report is 'under review.' By noon it's vanished. The room is more owned than you knew.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's open between you now — no more pretending. Martha's warmth has a blade under it. And she knows exactly how exposed you are.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You have proof now, and a secret that could get you killed. The next shift, Martha brings you coffee and watches you drink it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your report disappeared. Now you know the ring isn't in the house on Calder. It's in the building you work in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha shows up at your door with takeout. 'We should talk. Off the floor.'

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I'm not a monster. I send the warnings I can. I lose the files I have to. You think one rookie with a conscience can stop this? You'll just disappear into it. Like the files.

decision.prompt: Martha, in your doorway, asking you to understand

choices.label: Then help me stop it. Turn on them.
Say nothing. Let her think you'll fold.
Maybe you're right. Maybe I should look away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She leaves the takeout and a long, sad look. Whatever you said, you both know the mentorship died on that floor tonight.

plot_call.title: We're The Same
plot_call.synopsis: The Don offers you in — or marks you a liability.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A call routed straight to you. No caller ID. A man's voice, calm as a closing door.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Martha speaks highly of you. We can use someone with a conscience — they're so good at justifying things. Or we can use you another way. Your choice, dispatcher.

decision.prompt: The Don, in your ear, offering you 'in'

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: A liability, then. Pity. Tell your grandmother on Maple Court we said hello.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You keep him talking, fingers flying — and pull a tower hit before he cuts out. It's thin. It's something. It's the first thread that leads up, not down.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Simple. You keep dispatching like a hero. You just go slow on certain streets. Nobody dies who wasn't already gone. And you get whole.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He hangs up gently. The threat wasn't loud. It didn't have to be — he named Maple Court, and now you know they know about Grandma.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One tower, one timestamp. Not enough to arrest a shadow. Enough to prove the shadow is real.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't say yes. You don't say no. The silence is its own answer, and you both heard it.

weekend.title: A Nice Young Man
weekend.synopsis: They visited Grandma. Warn her or watch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Grandma calls, cheerful, oblivious. 'A nice young man came by asking about Lily. Said he was a coworker. Wasn't that kind?'

decision.prompt: They went to Grandma's door. She has no idea.

choices.label: Warn her. Carefully. Get her somewhere safe.
Don't scare her. Quietly watch her street.
Say nothing. You can't protect everyone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hang up and sit in the dark a long time. The job used to end when the shift did. It doesn't anymore.

plot_call.title: The Coded Call
plot_call.synopsis: A test from the Don, with Grandma as collateral.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A call comes in sounding ordinary — a noise complaint. But the words are off, rehearsed. A code, and you're meant to answer it.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Unit to 1411 Calder, tonight, 2am. Confirm you understand by sending no one. A friend will leave something for you. Refuse, and a friend on Maple Court leaves instead.

decision.prompt: A test, with Grandma as the stake

choices.label: Wear a wire. Bait them. Build the case.
Send a unit to 1411 anyway, openly.
Send no one. Take the deal. Protect Grandma.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go to the investigators you still trust and come back wired. The next coded call, you play along — every word recorded. It's the bravest, most reckless thing you've done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You roll a marked car to 1411 at 2am. They scatter. No bust — but you've shown them you won't be tested. Martha won't look at you on the way out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You send no one. At dawn there's money and a note: 'Maple Court stays safe. So do you. Welcome.' You bought Grandma a week and sold something you won't get back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hours of the ring's own voices, recorded. The case stops being your private file and starts being a weapon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No arrests, but a message sent both ways. They know you're a wave now. And waves get managed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You're inside it now, the way Martha is — saving the city with one hand and steadying its worst with the other. It doesn't feel like a choice anymore.

weekend.title: The Mirror
weekend.synopsis: Who can you trust with this?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You haven't slept right in weeks. The mirror shows someone who's started flinching at their own phone.

decision.prompt: Who do you tell? You can't carry this alone.

choices.label: A trusted detective outside the building.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whatever you chose, you cross a line at the kitchen table: this stops being a job you survive and becomes a thing you intend to end.

plot_call.title: The Whisper
plot_call.synopsis: Lily escapes and calls you — with Martha six feet away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 1:50am. A call breaks through — barely a whisper, a girl hiding, hand over the mic. Martha is six feet away, headset on, watching her own board.

lines.speaker: lily
lines.text: I got out. I'm in the lot behind Calder, under a truck. Please don't say the address out loud. Please. They're inside. Is this — are you the one Gran talks about?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's Lily. Alive. And the one person who can't know is sitting right beside you.

choices.label: Type the unit silently. Keep Lily talking low.
Step away 'for a break,' call it in from the hall.
Loud and official — force Martha to react.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You key the unit by hand, no voice, eyes on your own screen. 'Stay with me, Lily. Help is moving. Don't hang up.' Martha shifts. Glances over. You smile and sip your coffee.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 'Bathroom,' you mouth. In the stairwell you call the rescue in clean. When you come back, Martha's eyes are on Lily's open line. 'Who's that?' she asks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You call it across the floor, full volume, by the book — so it can't be quietly buried. Martha's face goes white, then very still. The whole room is a witness now.

decision.prompt: Martha is one move from catching it. The unit is two minutes out.

choices.label: Hold the line. Cover Lily until the car arrives.
Panic. Hang up to protect yourself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Headlights swing into the lot. A real officer, not one of theirs. Lily's voice cracks — 'I see them, I see them' — and then she's crying, and safe. You bring Grandma's girl home from your console without ever raising your voice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hang up. The silence is unbearable. You tell yourself she'll call back. The line stays dark.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You burned the secret to save the girl. A clean unit reaches Lily — and the whole floor saw Martha flinch. You can't take it back, and neither can she.

weekend.title: Hospital Hallway
weekend.synopsis: The cost and the relief of the rescue.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If Lily made it out: a hospital hallway, Grandma's arms around a girl who keeps saying 'the dispatcher, the dispatcher.' If she didn't: a quiet you'll carry a long time.

choices.label: Sit with Grandma. Let it land.
Go straight back to the file. It's not over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One girl, maybe, out of the dark. But Calder still has its curtains, and Martha still has her console. This was a battle. The war is next.

plot_call.title: The Price
plot_call.synopsis: Retaliation: you're framed, and Grandma is watched.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Retaliation comes the way it always does here — quiet, deniable, devastating.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Funny thing happened. A unit got bad coordinates tonight. Rolled to the wrong address. An officer got hurt, and the paperwork points at your console, rookie. Your login. Your night.

decision.prompt: They're framing you to fold you

choices.label: Prove it was tampering. Pull the logs.
Go to the detective with everything, now.
Beg Martha to make it go away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You dig into the raw logs and find her fingerprints — an override stamped with credentials that aren't yours. The frame becomes evidence of the framer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hand it all over — the file, the wire if you have it, the logs. 'This is enough to move,' the detective says quietly. 'But once we move, you can't un-move. They'll come for everyone you've touched.'

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: There it is. That's the rookie I can keep whole. Stay small, stay quiet, and I'll bury the report. We protect our own here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The frame backfires. You don't just clear yourself — you catch Martha's hand on the override. The hunter, for one night, is the hunted.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's out of your hands now, and into the hands of someone who can act. The sting gets a green light. So does the danger.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The report vanishes. You keep your job, your record, your silence. Martha pats your shoulder. You've never felt so small, or so owned.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Grandma calls — there's a strange car parked on Maple Court two nights running. 'Probably nothing,' she says. You know better.

decision.prompt: They're reminding you what they can reach

choices.label: Get Grandma and Lily out of the city tonight.
Stake out the car. Get a plate, get proof.
You can't. You're too compromised to help her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whatever it cost you, the message is received: this ends one of two ways now. You break them, or they break everyone you love.

plot_call.title: The Trap
plot_call.synopsis: Run the sting from your console — beside Martha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything has led here. The detective's voice in your earpiece: 'We move tonight. But it only works if it runs through your console. You're the bait and the trigger.'

decision.prompt: Run the sting from your seat — beside Martha

choices.label: Bait the coded call. Feed them a fake unit gap.
Let Martha reroute the decoy — then catch her live.
Tip Martha off. You're too owned to go through with it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You seed the lie: a two-minute window, no units near Calder. The ring takes the bait and moves — straight into a street full of waiting officers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You watch Martha's hands. She takes the decoy, mislabels it, texts the address — and every keystroke goes to the detective in real time. She builds the case against herself, one habit at a time.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Good. Good. I told them you'd choose right. Now sit still and let the grown-ups work.

decision.prompt: Martha feels it turning. Her hand moves toward the master line.

choices.label: Lock the board. Don't let her warn them.
Look her in the eye and let her decide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You freeze the console before she can key the warning. On the street, the trap closes. In the room, Martha slowly takes off her headset and sets it down, like she's been waiting years to.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hold her gaze. For a second she could blow it all up. Instead her hand falls away. 'I was your age once,' she says. 'Nobody locked the board for me.' She lets it happen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sting collapses. Two officers compromised, the ring melts back into the dark, and your name is on the failure. You didn't just stay a pawn. You became the wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: However it broke, tomorrow is the last shift of this. You sit with the file — pages of it now, or a thin folder, or nothing but a sticky note.

choices.label: Read it all one more time. Be ready.
Call Grandma. Tell her tomorrow it ends.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't sleep. You don't need to. Tomorrow the frequency goes loud, one way or another.

plot_call.title: Open Frequency
plot_call.synopsis: Climax and four endings on a final choice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Last shift. The board is yours. Whatever you've become, it all comes down to the next thing you choose to do with this frequency.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Don's number lights up your console one final time — the last loose end, asking what kind of dispatcher you turned out to be.

choices.label: Blow the whistle. Put it all on the record, live.
Take the throne. The ring needs a new inside ear.
Cut the deal: their freedom for the girls' safety.
Say nothing. Close the lines. Walk away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ENDING — THE WHISTLE. You open every line at once and read it into the record where it can't be buried: names, addresses, the override logs, Martha's keystrokes. By dawn the house on Calder is taped off, the Don's number is a case number, and Martha is led past your console without a word. Lily comes home for good. The frequency, for the first time, is clean. It cost you everything quiet in your life. You'd do it again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ENDING — THE PAWN. You take the seat Martha kept warm. You're a hero on paper — commendations, clean dispatches, the city's trust — and the ear the ring relies on in the dark. The vans still run on Calder. You just make sure no one official ever hears them. You got whole. You're not sure what's left inside the wholeness.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ENDING — LOOSE THREADS. You trade what you have for what you can save: the Don walks, Martha vanishes before the cuffs, but the houses empty out and the girls — most of them — get to go home. It isn't justice. It's a ledger that balances barely in the black. You learn to live with barely. Some nights it's enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ENDING — DEAD AIR. You close the lines and walk out into the morning. No headlines, no arrests, no record that any of it happened. Calder Street keeps its curtains. Somewhere a phone rings into a console that nobody's watching anymore, and the city never learns the difference. Martha was right about one thing: it ate the rookie whole.

weekend.title: After
weekend.synopsis: Grandma's last word. The frequency stays open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: After. The shift ends, the way every shift ends — with the hum, and the lines, and whatever you can carry home.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Whatever happened in there, I want you to know: you picked up. When it mattered, a real person picked up. That's more than this city usually gives a frightened old woman and her girl.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hang up. The console is dark. Out there, the frequency is still open — full of voices, some of them wanting saving, some of them not. Tomorrow someone has to learn the difference. Tonight, it was you.

tag_legend.week_min: earliest week this call can appear
tag_legend.unit: correct unit: fire | police | ambulance | animal_control | none

library.title: My Kitchen's on Fire

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Split screen: you at the console; on the other end, a kitchen vanishing into orange smoke.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: My kitchen is on fire! 🔥

choices.label: Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: WHAT?! This is an EMERGENCY!

choices.label: And emergencies are what we do 😎
Sorry. Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: No, it's way too hot!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I can't get out, it's too hot!

choices.label: Get out of the house NOW.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I need someone, please!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: 989 Burb Street.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sirens. The truck rounds the corner before the roof gives. The city breathes a little easier.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Citizen trust ticks up. Clean.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A patrol car at a house fire. The city notices, and not in a good way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You let it burn. The city will feel that one.

library.title: I'm Out of Toilet Paper

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An anguished voice, echoing off bathroom tile. The camera, if there were one, would rather not come in.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: HELP! I'm out of toilet paper!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I don't care.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I'm barefoot!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Please, I pooped!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: So are you sending toilet paper?

choices.label: Yeah, I'll wipe for you too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nicely handled. Good judgment pays, and the city cracks a smile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little too cheeky — but you filtered it. Counts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Call dropped. No pay, no problem.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A unit for toilet paper — tied up all afternoon, with the city watching.

library.title: I Lost Everything in Bitcoin

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in front of a screen of red, plunging charts. He dials a number he shouldn't.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I bought bitcoin and lost everything.

choices.label: Yikes. What are you gonna do?
Hey, chin up, it'll be okay.
